question.:question/problem:
Given that $x=4\sqrt{y}+3{y}^{5},$ express $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ as a function of $y.$
$\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=$ {{field-1}} $2\sqrt{y}\,+${{field-2}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(4\sqrt{y}+3{y}^{5}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(4{y}^{1/2}+3{y}^{5}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(4{y}^{1/2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(3{y}^{5}) \\  & =2{y}^{-1/2}+15{y}^{4} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{y}}+15{y}^{4} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{y}}{y}+15{y}^{4} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{y}+15{y}^{5}}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y}\right)}^{-1}=\frac{y}{2\sqrt{y}+15{y}^{5}}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Given that $x=-\frac{2}{{y}^{2}}+5{y}^{2},$ express $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ as a function of $y.$
$\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=$ ${y}^{3}$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-\frac{2}{{y}^{2}}+5{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-2{y}^{-2}+5{y}^{2}) \\  & =-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-2})+5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =-2(-2{y}^{-3})+5(2y) \\  & =\frac{4}{{y}^{3}}+10y \\  & =\frac{4+10{y}^{4}}{{y}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y}\right)}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{3}}{4+10{y}^{4}}.
$$
